summary: Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1947) and under Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University from circa 1970 to 1996.

Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a research fellow at Tribhuvan University and served as a professor at Koyasan University, where his posts are attested in 1970 and 1984–1985.

Historian and Indologist Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) served as Honorary Director (attested 1959–1966) and Joint Director (attested 1987) at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute. He was also Vice-Chancellor at Patna University (attested 1973).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and under Sylvain Lévi. An Indologist and historian, he taught at Scottish Church College, held a post at Calcutta, and served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society.
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani. She held an academic post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Kalpana Ram is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University (1981–1989), where she held an attested post in 2026.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling under teachers including Norbu Tondrup. He served as Palpung's Vajra Master and as Abbot of Changchub Choeling Monastery.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and Sinology. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and served as an Emeritus Professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
Kamal K. Sridhar is an Indologist and linguist associated with Stony Brook University. She served there as a director (attested 2007) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Kamala Tiyavanich works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. During his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Bonn, the University of Toronto (~1967–1968), and Brown University (~1968–1970).

Kameshwar Nath Mishra worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a post as professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and was a visiting research scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Charles University. He held posts at the Czech Oriental Institute, Charles University, and Utrecht University, with visiting professorships at Chicago, Heidelberg, and Collège de France.

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, University of the Punjab, University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University. She subsequently held academic appointments at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University (~1968–1970).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (d. 2023), a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Dean at Banaras Hindu University (~1960–1998), Chairman of the Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor at IGNCA (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (b. 1965) is an archaeology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Su Bai. He has served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune. He served as Lecturer in Pali at Calcutta University (attested 1982).
Kanchu Onoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and later served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yün-hua Jan. He held an academic post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
